document.title: Excerpt from Record of Conversation between Mikhail Gorbachev and James Baker, February 9, 1990
document.authors: Gorbachev Foundation / Bush Presidential Library record
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: In Moscow, Baker and Gorbachev discuss an Afghan political settlement. Both prefer a political solution and independent Afghanistan but admit limited influence over Afghan parties. Gorbachev promotes the Najibullah plan of UN-monitored elections; Baker says the Mujahedin cannot be persuaded. Both say 'let them boil in their own juices'.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: Soviet leader (General Secretary of the CPSU), speaking with US Secretary of State

mentions.quote: Let them boil in their own juices over there. Maybe something will come out. We are now more on the sidelines.
We are in favor of political settlement in Afghanistan. And there is just one individual, one person, who stands in the way
Najubullah supports holding Shura, but in Kabul.

persons.name: Najibullah
persons.role: President of the Kabul government and PDPA leader

mentions.quote: we are not demanding that Najibullah step down before the start of the process.

organizations.name: Mujahedin
organizations.notes: Baker says US influence over them is limited; he refers to fundamentalists among them.

organizations.name: PDPA
organizations.notes: Baker wants Najibullah and closest associates, not the entire PDPA, to leave.

organizations.name: Afghan interim government
organizations.notes: Baker concedes it is also not quite legitimate.

organizations.name: Pakistan
organizations.notes: US claims certain influence over it.

organizations.name: Saudi Arabia
organizations.notes: Baker hopes to win its support for the settlement process.

organizations.name: United Nations
organizations.notes: Shevardnadze says Najibullah wants elections under UN auspices.

events.description: Gorbachev and Baker discuss an Afghan political settlement and the future of Najibullah.
Baker and Shevardnadze held negotiations on Afghanistan the day before.
Gorbachev and Baker discuss Afghan settlement, Najibullah's departure, and a Shura.
Shevardnadze and Baker held negotiations the previous day, discussing Afghanistan.
Najibullah tried twice to convene a Shura without success.
The Mujahedin also tried to convene a Shura and failed.

relationships.detail: Najibullah is treated as the leader of the PDPA regime in Kabul, with the US wanting him and his closest associates to go.
relationships.quote: he and his closest associates, not even the entire PDPA, will leave the stage.

relationships.detail: They negotiated on Afghanistan the day before.
relationships.quote: E. A. Shevardnadze told me that you had a good conversation about Afghanistan

relationships.detail: Baker met Gorbachev and discussed an Afghan settlement.
relationships.quote: Record of Conversation between Mikhail Gorbachev and James Baker

relationships.detail: Baker claims US influence over Pakistan.
relationships.quote: we have certain influence over Pakistan

relationships.detail: Baker calls Najibullah a man installed by foreign troops.
relationships.quote: this man, installed by foreign troops, would leave the stage.

relationships.detail: Baker links Pakistan and Saudi Arabia with the Mujahedin and the process.
relationships.quote: the main Mujahedin leaders, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to support the process

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze had a good conversation with Baker about Afghanistan, reported to Gorbachev.
relationships.quote: E. A. Shevardnadze told me that you had a good conversation about Afghanistan but that there was not much movement.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze said that after the previous day's negotiations there was a basis for discussions with the United States.
relationships.quote: After yesterday’s negotiations I had an impression that we have the basis for discussions with the United States.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze reported to Gorbachev on his Afghanistan talks with Baker.
relationships.quote: E. A. Shevardnadze told me that you had a good conversation about Afghanistan

relationships.detail: Baker speaks on behalf of the U.S. in the conversation.
relationships.quote: On our part, we have moved, but not enough for you.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev speaks for the USSR on Afghan policy.
relationships.quote: Because starting from Afghanistan, we started to implement a new approach to regional conflicts

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze acts for the Soviet side in negotiations.
relationships.quote: After yesterday’s negotiations I had an impression that we have the basis for discussions

relationships.detail: Baker says US influence over the Mujahedin is limited.
relationships.quote: Our influence on the Mujahedin is limited.

relationships.detail: Baker says the U.S. has certain influence over Pakistan.
relationships.quote: we have certain influence over Pakistan.

relationships.detail: Najibullah is treated as the leader of the PDPA regime; Baker wants him and his associates to leave, not the whole PDPA.
relationships.quote: he and his closest associates, not even the entire PDPA, will leave the stage.

relationships.detail: Baker calls Najibullah the one individual standing in the way of settlement and wants him to leave.
relationships.quote: there is just one individual, one person, who stands in the way of this settlement.

relationships.detail: Baker describes Najibullah as installed by foreign troops.
relationships.quote: this man, installed by foreign troops, would leave the stage.

relationships.detail: Najibullah's government is in Kabul and wants Shura held there.
relationships.quote: Najubullah supports holding Shura, but in Kabul.

relationships.detail: The interim government is grouped with the main Mujahedin leaders.
relationships.quote: convince the Afghan interim government, the main Mujahedin leaders, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia

relationships.detail: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are treated as backers whose support is needed alongside Mujahedin leaders.
relationships.quote: the main Mujahedin leaders, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to support the process

relationships.detail: Saudi Arabia is among parties to be convinced to support the settlement process.
relationships.quote: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to support the process of creating first a transitional government

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze says Najibullah wants elections under UN auspices.
relationships.quote: he wants these elections to be held under the UN auspices.

sources_cited: Record of Conversation between Mikhail Gorbachev and James Baker, 9 February 1990 (Gorbachev Foundation / Bush Presidential Library)
key_claims: Baker says US influence on the Mujahedin is limited, though it has some influence over Pakistan.
The US wants a guarantee that Najibullah and his closest associates leave power at the end of a transition, not necessarily before the process starts.
Baker says the US has no interest in a victory of the fundamentalists or in an Afghan government hostile to the USSR.
Baker admits the Afghan interim government is not quite legitimate either.
Gorbachev says the USSR is on the sidelines and cannot give orders, but cares about the reputational aspect of an Afghan settlement.
Najibullah supports a Shura held in Kabul and, per Shevardnadze, elections under UN auspices; Baker says the Mujahedin would not accept elections under Najibullah.
